First connection? In Windows VR Host Manager, choose Pair headset. Here, choose Set up PC, compare the code and approve once on the PC.

Two streaming modes share this build. Both need a companion program running on the PC the headset or phone talks to. Pick the mode that matches your use case; the section below covers both.

Screen gaming streams PC games to a virtual screen on the headset or phone. The PC runs Sunshine (or Apollo, an alternative Sunshine-based host). The headset client pairs with the host over the local network.
Install Sunshine (or Apollo) on the PC and launch it.
The host is now discoverable over the local network.
Run Screen gaming on the headset.
Pick the discovered PC (or Add PC by address).
The headset shows a PIN. Open the Sunshine (or Apollo) web UI on the PC and enter that PIN to pair.
Pick the game or Desktop entry in the app list to start streaming.
Stream SteamVR with head and Touch controller tracking. Install the matching custom Windows host from this app release. Stock ALVR builds cannot connect to this preview.
Install VibertemisVR Host Manager from this release. Keep your existing Vibeshine installation for screen gaming.
Open Host Manager and choose Set up VR. It checks the Windows runtime automatically; approve setup when prompted.
If Steam or SteamVR needs setup, use the displayed action, then retry Set up VR. Close SteamVR and ALVR Dashboard first.
Enable Keep host ready after Windows sign-in. Leave the manager in the tray; SteamVR starts when you connect for VR.

Choose Pair headset in Windows VR Host Manager. On this app’s home screen, choose Set up PC and select your PC. Compare every character of the code and approve on the PC once. No pairing file is required.
Choose Connect, grant microphone access, and confirm any restart. Save running VR games first.
Once connected, launch a VR game from the SteamVR library in the headset.
This preview build requires microphone permission to start SteamVR. You can control voice chat in the ALVR dashboard.

Remote VR needs a reachable PC route: a VPN on both devices, or a public address with the VR ports forwarded correctly. Select the reachable adapter under Windows Advanced and repeat Set up VR. Forwarded GameStream ports alone do not carry tracked VR.

PCVR settings offers PyroWave for Home, Standard AV1/HEVC, Travel mode and bitrate limits. Home allows up to 200 Mbps; Travel starts at 30 Mbps. Use ALVR Dashboard for resolution, refresh and fixed foveation. Start at 72 Hz and test your network.

If setup fails, check that the matching Windows VR Host Manager is hosting and reachable. Reopen Pair headset on the PC, then choose Set up PC here to retry. Vibeshine needs no changes. Manual pairing remains under Advanced.

Microphone access is required before PCVR can start. If the system permission dialog no longer appears, open this app\'s system settings to grant Microphone permission, then tap SteamVR (PCVR) again.

Apply one of the bundled Home, Travel, or High quality LAN screen-streaming presets. Each preset only changes resolution, fps, bitrate, and codec. Other settings (depth, frame pacing, inputs) stay where they are. Custom preserves your current values.
2560x1440 @ 72 fps, 40 Mbps, codec Auto. A reasonable starting point for a quiet wired or Wi-Fi 6 LAN.
1920x1080 @ 60 fps, 17 Mbps, codec Auto. Conservative values for cellular or hotel Wi-Fi; raw bandwidth is not the only factor.
3840x2160 @ 60 fps, 80 Mbps, codec Auto. For very fast wired LANs. Higher bitrates are available manually; 80 Mbps does not guarantee a stutter-free stream.
Saves the selection \"Custom\" only. Your currently configured streaming settings (resolution, fps, bitrate, codec) are not touched.

Pair your PC and choose codec, Travel mode and bitrate limits. Resolution, refresh rate and fixed foveation remain in ALVR Dashboard.
Enabled for connections from this app. Set separate Home and Travel limits in PC pairing and codec; bitrate adapts below the selected limit.
Downscales the periphery of each frame before encoding. Centre detail is preserved; peripheral detail is reduced. There is no measured savings guarantee.
Choose experimental PyroWave or Standard AV1/HEVC in PC pairing and codec. Runtime capabilities determine the actual stream codec; settings apply on the next connection.
Set on the ALVR dashboard. The actual headset refresh the runtime uses depends on the dashboard setting and the headset firmware.
Set on the ALVR dashboard. The render target is the per-eye desktop resolution the streamer is asked for, not a fixed overshoot of the headset panel.
Quest 3 has no eye-tracking hardware. Gaze-driven foveation is not available; only fixed-foveated encoding is.
